Cc: emily.chen@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-02-16T14:08:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode & cost questions

Hey Aditya —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap / asks from our side:

- Primary use case: clinical triage assistant integrated into our existing EHR workflow.
- Peak concurrent requests: ~120 qps on weekday mornings; typical baseline ~25 qps.
- Latency expectation: P95 < 350ms for chat completions.
- Data residency: must stay within our VPC for PHI-sensitive content, at least for training-ish datasets and logs.

We wanted a clearer sense of the cost tradeoffs between: Hosted API (per-token), Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commits), and Private VPC / on-prem options. Specifically:

1) Rough per-month cost estimate for each option given our traffic pattern (baseline + 4x peak bursts)
2) How reserved commits map to throughput guarantees (GPUs, throughput/slot assumptions)
3) Any approximate time-to-onboard for Private VPC (networking, security review)

Can you share a simple cost model and recommended deployment mode given the SLA/data constraints? Also loop in any intake SOW if helpful.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Lee
Director of Product, Integrations
AcmeHealth

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-16T17:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & cost questions

Jordan — great to connect. Appreciate the clear recap. See a short recap + next steps below and attached a lightweight cost model (AcmeHealth_cost_model.xlsx) and SOW stub (AcmeHealth_SOW_v2.pdf) for reference.

Recap / recommendation (high level):
- Given PHI/data residency requirements and your P95 latency target, Private VPC (customer-managed network) or Redwood Dedicated are the most realistic options. Hosted API can work for non-PHI traffic or prototypes, but you mentioned logs/data needing to remain within your VPC.
- If you need strict network isolation and on-prem options for audit, Private VPC/on-prem is recommended. Typical time-to-onboard: 6-10 weeks (security review, networking, KMS integration).
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) provides a faster path (2-4 weeks) with predictable throughput and SLA-backed latency if you reserve the right GPU pool. It also supports KMS and audit logging.

Cost model summary (see attached for numbers):
- Hosted API: pay-as-you-go per-token. Pros: fastest to start, no infra commitments. Cons: higher unit cost at sustained volume and not suitable for VPC-isolated PHI workloads unless combined with our Private offering.
- Dedicated: monthly commit for GPU capacity. Pros: lower per-token equivalent at sustained load, predictable monthly bill, SLA. Cons: commit needed; incremental burst costs possible.
- Private/VPC: one-time setup + recurring infra fee (or on-prem licensing). Pros: full data control, KMS/HSM options, compliant. Cons: longer onboarding and variable infra ops.

Requested next steps:
1) Can you confirm the typical daily token volumes (avg tokens per request) and expected growth over 6 months? I used conservative 45k tokens/day in the spreadsheet - if you can share exact numbers we'll update.
2) If Dedicated looks interesting, we'll run a small throughput sizing (what GPU type, expected seq lengths) and map to reserved slots.
3) If Private/VPC is required, we'll schedule a security kickoff (SLA, network topology, KMS).

Sincerely,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: AcmeHealth_cost_model.xlsx (spreadsheet), AcmeHealth_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW stub)

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & cost questions - updated model (Dedicated vs Hybrid)

Emily / Jordan - thanks for the details. I updated the spreadsheet and included two scenarios inline here for quick visibility; full workbook attached. Numbers are ballpark - we can swap in your actual token/day later.

Scenario A - Dedicated (reserve for peak + 20% buffer):
- Assumptions: avg tokens/request = 380; average req/sec baseline 25; peak 120 qps for 15 min bursts x 5 per day = ~12,000 burst requests/day. Sequence length avg = 1.2k tokens per session (including context + response).
- Throughput sizing: 4x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs (continuous) gives ~140 qps sustained for chat-like workloads after batching optimizations and KV cache warmup. That meets your 120 qps peak with ~16% buffer.
- Cost: Reserved capacity @ 4x A100-eq = $78,000/month (commit + infra fee). Estimated token-equivalent unit cost = ~$0.0035/token at sustained volume.
- Pros/cons: Predictable cost and SLA. Requires monthly commit. Faster onboarding (2-4 weeks).

Scenario B - Hybrid (Dedicated for real-time + Private VPC for logs/offline):
- Setup: Dedicated (2x A100-eq) sized for steady-state + small bursts, autoscale to private pool or burst capacity during peaks; Private VPC used for ingesting and storing PHI logs, plus an on-prem training pipeline for long-term models.
- Throughput sizing: 2x A100-eq Dedicated covers baseline + modest bursts (sustained ~70 qps). For the remaining peak capacity, we configure burst policies to route overflow to a dedicated private pool or temporarily increase reserved capacity (auto-burst) during defined windows.
- Cost: Dedicated reserve (2x A100-eq) = $41,500/month + Private VPC baseline fee of $9,500/month + occasional burst usage. Effective average token-equivalent cost ~ $0.0047/token (hybrid mixes infra and per-token).
- Pros/cons: Lower upfront commit, faster initial delivery, full control over PHI logs. Slightly more complex routing and ops.

Next recommended steps:
1) If you want to prototype quickly, sign the SOW (attached) for a 3-month Dedicated trial at 2x A100-eq with an option to convert to 4x if we see sustained peak. We'll include a migration plan to Private VPC in month 2-3.
2) We'll schedule a sizing call with infra (30-45 minutes) to validate seq lengths, batching potential, and expected token/day.
3) Security kickoff if you confirm Private VPC requirement; we'll share the checklist (network CIDR, KMS preferences, logging retention).

I'll update the workbook with exact reserved commit numbers and a line-item breakdown. Let me know which scenario you want moved to the SOW and I'll push a DocuSign link.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
